open_questions: Source: Afton's own HiTEC 12204L PDS 'HiTEC® 12204L HDEO Additive Package', printed edition '06/17' (© 2017 Afton Chemical Corporation; PDF created 2017-06-16), retrieved as the Internet Archive original-bytes copy captured 2020-10-23 (SHA-256 7a1e57d81d66b52b83215da261732256867d89b651c75334068022362a74183e), p.2 (p.1 is the cover). Afton's live site blocks automated access. The same document is the source of AFTON_HITEC_12250. The archive's HiTEC 12200 bulletin DL2-14639.pdf (08/18) prints no HiTEC 12204L properties; it is used only for the premix formula and route context (see below).

Identity (ID-13): the inventory and identity review describe HiTEC 12204L as a premix defined in DL2-14639.pdf. Afton's own PDS presents it as 'HiTEC® 12204L HDEO Additive Package', 'part of the HiTEC 12200 family of products', with its own Typical Characteristics column and treat rate, so it is recorded as a product in its own right. HiTEC 12204Y and HiTEC 12252 are separate inventory materials; nothing from them is used.

Premix formula, not a treat rate: DL2-14639.pdf p.2 (08/18) footnote 1 '14.2% HiTEC® 12204L = 10.3% HiTEC® 12200 + 4.2% HiTEC® 12250', attached to the approvals row '10.3%¹ | 4.2% HiTEC® 12250 | SAE 15W-40 | GP II' (the 05/18 bulletin DL2-11412.PDF p.2 prints the same footnote). The PDS (06/17, p.2) says 'The performance level of HiTEC® 12204L can also be achieved through the use of HiTEC® 12250 booster package at 4.2% in combination with HiTEC® 12200 at 10.3%'. This is an alternative two-product route for SAE 15W-40 (GP II in DL2-14639), equivalent to 14.2% HiTEC® 12204L; it is not a general treat rate or a required co-component of HiTEC® 12204L, so it is recorded here only. 10.3% + 4.2% = 14.5%, not the printed 14.2% (also noted in AFTON_HITEC_12250); recorded as printed, not reconciled. Confirm with Afton.

Claims printed for the equivalent route only: DL2-14639.pdf p.2 (08/18) marks API SL, API SJ and DDC 93K214 in the row '10.3%¹ | 4.2% HiTEC® 12250 | SAE 15W-40 | GP II'. These columns do not exist in the 06/17 PDS approvals band, so they are not added to HiTEC® 12204L's claims and not treated as conflicts (columns absent, not contradicted). Confirm with Afton whether they apply to HiTEC® 12204L.

MAN 3275: the PDS footnote reads '*:Equivalent performance. MAN 3275 now obsolete' (claim_type 'other'); DL2-14639.pdf footnote 5 for the equivalent route reads 'Meets requirements of (MRO)'. The wordings differ but do not contradict each other; not recorded as a conflict.

Deutz labels are recorded as printed in the PDS: 'Deutz DDQ-III' and 'Deutz DCQ-II'. DL2-14639.pdf prints 'Deutz DQC- III' and 'Deutz DQC- II'. Probably the same specifications; not confirmed, not normalized.

Claim type: all 20 columns sit under the printed header 'Approvals', including API CI-4 Plus, API CI-4, API CH-4 and ACEA E7-16, so claim_type = 'approval' (same reading as AFTON_HITEC_12200). Please confirm this reading.

Intended service, permitted base oils, route restrictions, required co-components and published formulations are not printed; left Missing. The bar charts on p.2 (Mack T-12, Cat 1K, Seq IIIF, Mack T-11 '*Based on % Soot at 12 cSt' vs 'API CI-4 Plus Limit' / 'Reserve') have no numeric values, and the field-test text ('field tested in harsh conditions to 50,000km/31,000 miles') refers to the HiTEC 12200 family; neither is recorded.

conflicts.note: HiTEC 12204L PDS 06/17 vs HiTEC 12200 bulletin 08/18 (equivalent two-product route). The field records the PDS marking, which is the product's own document; the DL2-14639 marking refers to the 10.3% + 4.2% route. Not resolved; confirm with Afton.
